title: The Rotor and the Wall: the Turbine Governor, the Enigma, and the Grave That Is Gone
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Frankfurt am Main: A Merchant's Son on the Modern Curriculum

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, birth in a house of accounts
stops.date_confidence: attested. Deutsche Biographie (gnd127822089) and de.wikipedia both give 30 October 1878; a rival 16 October date circulates in institutional popularizations and is unsupported by the stronger biographical record. The father's trade is corrected here from the dossier's 'financial broker' to Kaufmann, per the NDB genealogy ('V Gustav, Kaufm. in F.'); the Camphausen descent is the NDB's own.
stops.campa: In a merchant's household in Frankfurt am Main a son is born and registered as Jacob Ludolf Arthur Scherbius. His father Gustav keeps a trade in goods and credit; his mother Hedwig, born Nacken, descends from the Rhenish banker and minister Ludolf Camphausen, and the boy's middle name carries that descent forward into a house of accounts. The German Empire is seven years old and Frankfurt has been Prussian for twelve. Nothing here points at ciphers. The trade is invoices and bills of exchange.
suggested_refs: Deutsche Biographie genealogy for Gustav Scherbius (1836-1907) and Hedwig Nacken (1854-1954), with the descent from Ludolf Camphausen (1803-1890)

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the Oberrealschule and a year among machines
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the schooling (Deutsche Biographie: primary school and Oberrealschule at Frankfurt, 1885-1898, Abitur 1898); the month is a convention for the school year. The factory year is attested in substance by Deutsche Biographie, which states he worked briefly at a machinery factory before beginning study, but the firm is unidentified and the source does not say the factory was in Frankfurt: the coordinate is an assumption, flagged as such.
stops.campa: For thirteen years he goes to school in the city he was born in: primary school first, then the Oberrealschule, the modern track, where mathematics and the natural sciences take the hours a Gymnasium spends on Greek and Latin. He passes the Abitur in 1898 at nineteen. He does not go straight to a university. He spends about a year in a machinery factory instead, handling the machines rather than the mathematics of them. Which factory, and in which town, the source that records the year does not say.
suggested_refs: The Oberrealschule curriculum of the 1890s, the non-classical track that fed the technical universities
sources: en.wikipedia, 'Arthur Scherbius', citing the Neue Deutsche Biographie chronology

segments.name: Hanover and Munich: The Diploma and the Water-Turbine Governor

stops.name: Technische Hochschule Hannover, matriculation in electrical engineering
stops.date_confidence: source conflict, carried unresolved. de.wikipedia, drawing on university records, has him at TH Hannover 1899-1903, 'interrupted by two semesters at TH Munchen (1901-1902)'. Deutsche Biographie instead begins him at Munich in 1899, continues at institutions including Zurich, and brings him to Hannover only for the 1903 diploma. This file follows the record-based account and prints the other. The Zurich period is unconfirmed anywhere else and is given no stop. Month is the conventional start of the winter semester.
stops.campa: He matriculates in electrical engineering at the Technische Hochschule Hannover, in the Welfengarten buildings, and the discipline he enters is barely twenty years old as a university subject. Germany is wiring itself: alternating current against direct, the great machine firms hiring faster than the schools can graduate. He will spend four years here, with an interruption in Bavaria, and leave with a diploma in a field whose entire industrial vocabulary was invented inside his own lifetime.
suggested_refs: Matriculation registers of the Technische Hochschule Hannover, the basis of the de.wikipedia chronology

stops.name: Technische Hochschule Munchen, two semesters on the Arcisstrasse
stops.date_confidence: attested by de.wikipedia as two semesters at TH Munchen in 1901-1902, interrupting the Hannover years; the exact terms are not specified, and the month is the conventional start of the winter semester. Deutsche Biographie's account, which makes Munich the beginning rather than the interruption, is recorded on the Hannover stop.
stops.campa: Two semesters in Munich, at the Technische Hochschule on the Arcisstrasse, break the Hannover years in the middle. The Bavarian school is the one German polytechnic that rivals Hannover in electrical engineering, and students move between them as a matter of course. What he studies here is not separately recorded. He comes back north to finish. Whether he also spent a period at Zurich, as one biographical tradition holds, is a question the university records do not settle.
suggested_refs: The old main building of the Technische Hochschule Munchen on the Arcisstrasse

stops.name: Hannover, the Diplom-Ingenieur
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested by Deutsche Biographie, en.wikipedia and de.wikipedia alike; the month is not recorded anywhere reached, and June is chosen only to order the segment ahead of the autumn appointment at Frankfurt.
stops.campa: He takes the Diplom-Ingenieur at Hannover, twenty-four years old, trained in the machines that turn water and steam and coal into current. The subject that will hold him for the rest of his working life is already the one that interests him here: regulation. Not how to make a machine run, but how to make it hold a speed, a voltage, a state, against a load that changes without warning. The dissertation he will defend a year from now is about exactly that. He leaves Hannover with a post already waiting for him at Frankfurt.
suggested_refs: The Welfengarten buildings of the Technische Hochschule Hannover, where both the diploma and the doctorate are taken

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, project engineer at the Lahmeyerwerke
stops.date_confidence: attested by Deutsche Biographie as his first post-diploma position, at Felten & Guilleaume-Lahmeyerwerke, from 1903; Deutsche Biographie gives no town, and the Frankfurt pin follows the firm's Lahmeyer works there. The month is not attested.
stops.campa: He returns to Frankfurt as a project engineer at the Felten & Guilleaume-Lahmeyerwerke, one of the great cable and electrical concerns of the Rhine-Main region. It lasts about a year, and it is the only stretch of his career in which he is plainly an employee of a large company doing what large companies do. The work is the ordinary work of the profession: installations laid out, loads calculated, drawings answered for on a schedule somebody else has set.
suggested_refs: Felten & Guilleaume-Lahmeyerwerke, the Rhine-Main cable and electrical concern

stops.name: Hannover, the Dr.-Ing. for an indirectly acting governor
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Deutsche Biographie and en.wikipedia: the Dr.-Ing. conferred 14 July 1904 by the Technische Hochschule Hannover for a dissertation on the construction of an indirectly acting water-turbine governor. One of the few exact dates in the early life.
stops.campa: The Technische Hochschule Hannover confers the Dr.-Ing. on the fourteenth of July for a dissertation on the construction of an indirectly acting governor for water turbines. The problem is old and unglamorous: a turbine driving a generator must hold its speed while the demand at the far end of the line rises and falls all day, and a governor acting directly on the gate is too weak, too slow, or too violent. His answer is a mechanism that works through an intermediary, amplifying a small signal into a large controlled motion. He is twenty-five.
suggested_refs: Scherbius's 1904 Hannover dissertation on the indirectly acting water-turbine governor

segments.name: The Regulator: Berlin, Baden, and the Scherbius Cascade

stops.name: Berlin, a short season inside Siemens-Schuckert
stops.date_confidence: attested by Deutsche Biographie as a brief engineering post at Siemens-Schuckertwerke in 1904, followed by independent work from 1905; no address is attested and the month is not recorded. The dossier's Siemensstadt coordinate (52.5341, 13.2028) is discarded: it falls in Spandau Altstadt, and in 1904-05 Siemens-Schuckert was not yet concentrated at the Siemensstadt site of later fame. A generic Berlin pin is used deliberately, in place of false precision.
stops.campa: A brief post at the Siemens-Schuckertwerke in Berlin, and then he stops working for anyone. From 1905 he is an independent inventor and consulting engineer, which in the Germany of that decade is a real profession with a real market: firms buy solutions they have no department for, patents are property, and a man with a doctorate and a good idea can sell it. He will keep this footing for the rest of his life, in and out of companies, always with the patents in his own name until the year he signs them away.
suggested_refs: The German market for independent consulting engineers and patent-holders before 1914

stops.name: Baden, the slip power turned back into the motor
stops.date_confidence: attested by Deutsche Biographie and en.wikipedia; the employment at Brown, Boveri & Cie. in Baden spans roughly 1906 to 1912, and only the years are given, so the stop is dated to the start of the period with the month a placeholder.
stops.campa: At Brown, Boveri and Cie. in Baden he solves the problem that makes his professional name. Large induction motors run at one speed; industry wants them to run at any speed, and the power slipping away in the rotor is the waste that makes variable speed expensive. His circuits recover that slip power and feed it back, and the arrangement is called the Scherbius cascade, the one invention of his that carries his name while he is alive to hear it. It is used where the motors are biggest: rolling mills, mine hoists, pumps, ventilating fans.
suggested_refs: The Scherbius cascade, slip-power recovery for adjustable-speed polyphase induction motors

stops.name: Berlin, rectifiers, high-voltage direct current, and a machine never finished
stops.date_confidence: attested by Deutsche Biographie and en.wikipedia for the year 1912, when he returns to independent consulting in Berlin; the month is a placeholder, and no premises are attested, so the pin is central Berlin as a stated approximation.
stops.campa: He gives up Baden for Berlin and his own practice again. Mercury-vapour rectifiers, the glass bulbs in which an arc turns alternating current into direct; consulting work for Siemens; a scheme for high-voltage direct-current transmission decades before anyone builds one; and an ambitious direct-current machine that he never finishes. Some of what he designs in these years is built and sold; some of it stays on paper, and the direct-current machine is the piece that stays there.
suggested_refs: Mercury-arc rectifier development in the German electrical industry before 1914

stops.name: Berlin, radiators fired out of clay
stops.date_confidence: attested by Claus Taaks, HistoCrypt 2023, who dates it to 1914 and states the motive as contributing to the war effort rather than reacting to shortages; the dossier's [R] tag is upgraded here on that authority. The ceramics manufacturer and the works are genuinely unidentified, so the pin is generic Berlin and the location is a stated gap.
stops.campa: War comes, and he volunteers his trade to it. Working with a well-known ceramics manufacturer he develops processes for making radiators out of ceramic rather than metal, so that the metal can go elsewhere. The idea will follow him through the literature for a century as a curiosity, the cipher man's ceramic heating parts. He is thirty-six years old and has never worked on a cipher. Neither the manufacturer's name nor the works where the pieces were fired has been recovered by anyone since.
suggested_refs: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, on the 1914 ceramic radiator processes
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, pp. 170-180

segments.name: The Telegraph Troops and the Order That Is Lost

stops.name: Charleville-Mezieres, drafted to the wireless
stops.date_confidence: the draft into the telegraph troops in October 1915 is attested by Deutsche Biographie. The posting is not: Taaks 2023 says only that 'probably he was assigned to its directorate at the Grand Headquarters (GHQ). The telegraph troops were the only military unit whose command was at GHQ.' German GHQ in October 1915 stood at Charleville-Mezieres, and that pin is used in place of the dossier's 50.5, 6.5, which is empty country in the Eifel and corresponds to nothing.
stops.campa: He is drafted into the telegraph troops in October, thirty-seven years old, a doctor of engineering put into uniform for the one thing the army cannot buy on the open market: men who understand wireless. The telegraph troops are the only unit whose command sits at the Grand Headquarters, and that is probably where he serves. A colleague from the cipher bureau, writing it all down thirty years later for his interrogators, remembers him without needing to explain who he was.
stops.quote: the talented engineer Dr SCHERBIUS of the Supreme Army Command
stops.quote_source: Wilhelm Fenner, 'Die Geschichte der Chiffrierstelle' (1945), English translation TICOM DF-202, p. 9, quoted in Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, p. 170
suggested_refs: TICOM DF-202, Fenner's 1945 history of the German cipher bureau
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023

stops.name: Berlin, seconded to the procurement office
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Taaks 2023 and de.wikipedia: 1 February 1917, seconded to the Waffen- und Munitionsbeschaffungsamt as deputy head of a department, probably electrical machines and equipment. The premises are a gap: WuMBA's Berlin address is not established in anything reached, and the dossier's 52.5145, 13.376 falls inside the Tiergarten where no ministry stood. The pin approximates the War Ministry quarter on the Wilhelmstrasse and is not a located building.
stops.campa: On the first of February he is seconded out of field service and into the Waffen- und Munitionsbeschaffungsamt, the weapons and munitions procurement office, as deputy head of a department, probably the one for electrical machines and equipment. Within weeks of his arrival the War Ministry will ask him for a machine that enciphers by itself. For the moment it is a desk inside the war's supply machinery, and it puts him where requirements are written rather than where they are met.
suggested_refs: The Waffen- und Munitionsbeschaffungsamt (WuMBA) of the Prussian War Ministry
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023

stops.name: Berlin, the commission whose paper has never been found
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the fact, unrecoverable as to the content. Taaks 2023: 'In the spring of 1917, most likely at his transfer to the WuMBA, Scherbius received the order from the War Ministry to develop a cipher machine. The order itself and the specifications have not yet been found.' The dossier's specification, an automatic polyalphabetic cipher changing substitution after every keystroke, is therefore a modern inference read back out of the machine he built, not a documented requirement. Dated to spring, not to a day; April is an ordering device.
stops.campa: In the spring the order comes down from the Prussian War Ministry: develop a cipher machine. What the ministry actually asked for cannot be read, because neither the order nor its specifications has ever been found in any archive. Everything said about the requirement is read backwards out of the apparatus he built to meet it. Hand ciphers are failing all along the front, the traffic is enormous, and clerks encipher by table and by hand and make the errors the other side's bureaus live on. He is given the problem and no surviving instructions.
suggested_refs: The unrecovered 1917 War Ministry cipher-machine order, noted as missing in Taaks 2023
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023

stops.name: Partenkirchen, meeting Elisabeth Taaks
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The meeting at Partenkirchen and the engagement formalized at Frankfurt in June come from a family-document reconstruction relayed by the dossier; Taaks's HistoCrypt paper never mentions Elisabeth at all, and Deutsche Biographie carries no marriage information. de.wikipedia gives 'Elisabeth, geborene Taaks (1896-1945)', which makes her eighteen years his junior, not the nineteen the dossier states. Coordinate is Partenkirchen town; the Frankfurt engagement gets no separate stop.
stops.campa: At Partenkirchen, under the Wetterstein, he meets Elisabeth Adelaide Taaks. She is twenty-one, he is thirty-eight, and by the family's account they are engaged within weeks, the engagement formalized at Frankfurt in June. None of this appears in the archives that carry the rest of his life. It comes down through the family and through a genealogical line, and it is the point where the paper stops and the household begins. She will outlive him by sixteen years.
suggested_refs: The Scherbius family-document reconstruction relayed in the dossier chronology, unmatched by any archival source reached

stops.name: Bremen, the marriage in the third autumn of the war
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, dated to the day. The marriage at Bremen on 10 November 1917 and the witnesses Georg Taaks and Otto Christian Taaks come from de.wikipedia and the dossier's family reconstruction; Deutsche Biographie has no marriage entry, so the day rests on a single line of transmission. Coordinate is the Marktplatz district of Bremen, not a located register office.
stops.campa: They marry at Bremen on the tenth of November, in the third autumn of the war, her father Georg Taaks and her uncle Otto Christian Taaks standing as witnesses. Of the ceremony itself nothing comes down but the date and those two names. He is thirty-nine, a soldier for two years and a procurement official for nine months. In the same season he is at work on the apparatus that will be filed at the patent office fifteen weeks from now. The household they start here will end in a house at Wannsee seven years on.
suggested_refs: Bremen civil marriage register, 10 November 1917, not consulted directly

stops.name: Berlin, the foundational patent goes to the Gitschiner Strasse
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Crypto Museum patent index and the DPMA's own Enigma milestone page: filed 23 February 1918, granted as DE416219. Two corrections are carried here. The coordinate replaces the dossier's 52.5074, 13.3904 (Spittelmarkt, about 1.1 km wrong) with the Reichspatentamt's actual seat at Gitschiner Strasse, Kreuzberg, occupied since its 1905 new building. And the dossier's 'up to ten exchangeable rotors' is not in this filing: Taaks describes the demonstrator's 5x5 keys and 5x5 glow lamps, and the ten-rotor demand belongs to the navy, after April 1918.
stops.campa: The application goes in on the twenty-third of February. Wired wheels on a shaft; press a key and the current runs through the wheels by a path the wheels themselves alter at every stroke, so that the same letter does not encode to the same letter twice running. It is his first cipher patent and he is thirty-nine. It will not be published for another seven years, as DE416219. The demonstrator that goes with it carries a square of twenty-five keys and twenty-five glow lamps, five by five.
suggested_refs: DE416219, digitized and freely viewable via DEPATISnet and the Crypto Museum patent index
Bletchley Park's own institutional history page, which credits the invention to Scherbius by name
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023

stops.name: Spa, the demonstration announced to Great Headquarters
stops.date_confidence: attested as a letter, not as an eyewitness account: a Scherbius letter of 15 April 1918, cited in Taaks 2023, states that the demonstration will take place at Great Headquarters and afterwards before the Imperial Navy Office in Berlin. Great Headquarters was at Spa in Belgium from March 1918. The stop therefore carries the date of the announcement, and the demonstration is known through its own forecast.
stops.campa: He writes on the fifteenth of April that his two-rotor demonstrator is to be shown at the Great Headquarters, which since the spring has stood at Spa in the Belgian Ardennes, and afterwards to the Imperial Navy Office in Berlin. The officers who see it find the principle cryptographically strong, and what they ask for is more of it: more wheels and more paths before the cycle closes on itself. What survives is the letter announcing the demonstration, not any account of what happened at it.
suggested_refs: Scherbius's letter of 15 April 1918, cited in Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023

stops.name: Berlin, the navy asks for ten rotors and gets seven that fail
stops.date_confidence: attested as to substance by Taaks 2023, citing Bundesarchiv RM 5/3566: the naval command demanded ten rotors exchangeable on one axis in any order, and two seven-rotor machines built afterwards failed on unreliable electrical contacts. The month is not attested; May orders the stop after the letter of 15 April. Coordinate corrected from the dossier's 52.5145, 13.3628, which lands in the Tiergarten, to the Reichsmarineamt's new building on the north bank of the Landwehrkanal, occupied from 1914.
stops.campa: In the new naval building on the bank of the Landwehrkanal the machine is shown to the Imperial Navy Office, and the navy sets its terms: ten rotors, exchangeable on one axis in any order. Two seven-rotor machines are built to meet the demand and both fail, not cryptographically but mechanically. The war ends with the apparatus unadopted. Every rotor adds contacts, every contact is a place where the current can fail to pass, and a machine with that many sliding contacts cannot be relied on to say the same thing twice.
suggested_refs: Bundesarchiv RM 5/3566, the naval file on the seven-rotor trials, cited in Taaks 2023
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023

stops.name: Berlin, cipher elements moved by fluid
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Crypto Museum patent index and by Taaks 2023: filed 2 June 1918, later published as DE416833. Taaks supplies the afterlife of the idea: no such machine was built in Germany, but it was 'built in Britain in 1925 and 1926, in Czechoslovakia as first version of the Stolba-machine in 1930', with main patents by Koch 1919, Scherbius 1920, Sidney Hole 1922 and Sieber/Stolba. Same Reichspatentamt coordinate correction as the February filing.
stops.campa: A second application, four months after the first: cipher elements moved hydraulically or pneumatically instead of by ratchet and pawl, fluid where the first patent had metal fingers. No German machine is ever built on it. The idea travels anyway, into a British machine in 1925 and 1926 and into the first version of the Stolba machine in Czechoslovakia in 1930, and the tangle of pneumatic cipher patents from those years carries four names besides his own. He files it while the army that commissioned him is losing the war.
suggested_refs: DE416833; and the Koch, Hole and Sieber/Stolba pneumatic cipher patents that follow it
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023

stops.name: Berlin, liquidating a war and cutting seven rotors to three
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year by Deutsche Biographie and de.wikipedia: postwar consultancy to the Reichsverwertungsamt's armistice section and the Army Peace Treaty Commission, with the reduction from seven rotors to three or four and the turn toward a printing machine with a line-transposition stage. Month is a placeholder; the office coordinate is the dossier's and is not independently verified as a building.
stops.campa: The empire is gone and he is consultant to the offices that liquidate its war economy: the armistice section of the Reichsverwertungsamt, the army's peace treaty commission. The customer he built the cipher machine for no longer exists. In the same year he takes the failed apparatus apart and rebuilds it smaller: seven rotors come down to three or four, which the contacts can actually be relied on to carry, and he turns toward a machine that prints instead of lighting lamps, with a line-by-line scrambling stage added after the wheels.
suggested_refs: The Reichsverwertungsamt and the Army Peace Treaty Commission, the offices winding up the German war economy

segments.name: Scherbius & Ritter: Wannsee, Thermostats, and the Refusal

stops.name: Berlin-Wannsee, the firm at Konigstrasse 40
stops.date_confidence: founding date attested to the day by Taaks 2023: 'On 1st April the company Scherbius & Ritter was founded to develop and produce cipher machines and Birka controllers (thermostats) for household appliances.' The address in the dossier is wrong and is replaced: 'Schiffbauerdamm' appears nowhere in Taaks's paper, while de.wikipedia and gazette-berlin.de both place the firm in Wannsee, 'in der Konigstrasse 40'. Coordinate is Konigstrasse 40, 14109 Berlin. Taaks adds that Ritter's earlier firm, founded 1911, probably built the 1918 demonstrator.
stops.campa: On the first of April, out in Wannsee at the far southwestern edge of Berlin, he and Ernst Richard Ritter found the general partnership Scherbius und Ritter, at Konigstrasse 40. Ritter's own earlier firm probably built the two-rotor demonstrator of 1918. The premises will still be turning out thermostats and switches long after both founders are dead. The firm has two lines of business and they sit oddly beside each other: cipher machines on one side, and on the other Birka thermostats and electrically heated cushions for the household, sold under the name Scherip.
suggested_refs: Konigstrasse 40, Berlin-Wannsee, where gazette-berlin.de states the machine was developed in 1923
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023

stops.name: Berlin, the Reichspost declines and releases him
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: Reichspost letter to Scherbius, 13 August 1920, Bundesarchiv R 4701/8665, quoted in translation in Taaks 2023, p. 172. The coordinate approximates the Reichspost ministry quarter in Berlin-Mitte and is not a verified building footprint.
stops.campa: He offers the German state the patents outright. The answer comes back from the Reichspost in August, and it is the sentence the rest of the story turns on: no funds, and therefore no restriction. The state that commissioned the machine in 1917 will not buy it in 1920, and in the same breath it releases him to sell it abroad. Everything that follows follows from a budget line that was not there: the commercial machine, the journal article, the display cabinet in Stockholm, the export sales.
stops.quote: Unfortunately, the government is not in a position to spend funds on the purchase of your patents for a cipher machine. Consequently, the use of your invention is herewith released for foreign countries as well.
stops.quote_source: Reichspost official letter to Arthur Scherbius, 13 August 1920, Bundesarchiv R 4701/8665, translated in Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, p. 172
suggested_refs: Bundesarchiv R 4701/8665, the Reichspost file on the Scherbius cipher patents
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, p. 172

stops.name: Berlin, a writing machine that scrambles line by line
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Crypto Museum patent index and by Taaks 2023, who describes DE425147 more fully than the dossier does: the patent of a writing machine containing the line-by-line scrambling for pneumatic machines, rather than merely irregular movement of several cipher discs. Reichspatentamt coordinate corrected to Gitschiner Strasse as on the 1918 filings.
stops.campa: Another application at the Gitschiner Strasse office: a writing machine carrying the line-by-line scrambling, pneumatic drive among the concepts, granted later as DE425147. He is working two problems at once now, the stepping that resists analysis and the printing that would make the machine usable by a clerk rather than an operator reading lamps aloud to a second man. The patents accumulate faster than the orders. There are ten of them by the end of next year, and by then they will not be his.
suggested_refs: DE425147, the writing machine with line-by-line scrambling
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023

stops.name: Berlin, the December agreement and the silence after it
stops.date_confidence: attested from the administrative record via Taaks 2023: negotiations with the ministries through 1920, a demonstration on 2 December, an agreement with the Reichspost reportedly concluded 19 December, after which the project vanishes from the surviving papers with no evidence that any procurement was completed. The quoted companion letter from the Reich Telegraph Administration is dated only to 1920 (Bundesarchiv R 4701/8665). Coordinate as on the August stop, approximate.
stops.campa: The negotiations with the ministries run all year. There is a demonstration on the second of December and an agreement with the Reichspost concluded, by the record, on the nineteenth. Then the file goes quiet. No procurement follows, no delivery, no cancellation: the project simply stops appearing in the administrative papers that had been recording it up to that date. What the Reich Telegraph Administration had told him earlier in the year was that foreign inventors were moving and that he should hurry.
stops.quote: In view of the efforts of foreign inventors known to you for the introduction of cipher machines for telegraph operation, it can only be recommended that you speed up your work.
stops.quote_source: Reich Telegraph Administration letter to Arthur Scherbius, 1920, Bundesarchiv R 4701/8665, translated in Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, p. 172
suggested_refs: Bundesarchiv R 4701/8665; the competing machine of Arvid Gerhard Damm, implied in the warning
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, p. 172

stops.name: Berlin, ten patents signed over to Securitas
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Deutsche Biographie and Taaks: on 21 November 1921 ten cipher patents or applications pass to Gewerkschaft Securitas, a Berlin precision-engineering concern, against a minority interest and manufacturing cooperation for Scherbius and for Scherbius & Ritter. The package includes DE378238, filed 24 May 1921, for lamp indication of the shift between letters and figures (Crypto Museum). Securitas's offices are not located in anything reached; the pin is central Berlin and is a stated gap.
stops.campa: On the twenty-first of November he signs ten cipher patents and applications over to the Gewerkschaft Securitas, a Berlin precision-engineering concern, and takes in exchange a minority interest and an undertaking to manufacture. The package runs from the foundational 1918 filing down to the small ones, as small as the lamp that shows whether the machine is set for letters or for figures. From this day the inventions are a company's assets and he is a shareholder in them. He is forty-three.
suggested_refs: DE378238, lamp indication of the letter-figure shift, filed 24 May 1921
Gewerkschaft Securitas, Berlin
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023

stops.name: Berlin, the secret published by its own inventor
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day and in its interpretation by Taaks 2023: 'on 10th May 1922, DE385682 for electromechanical machines, the process that the Reichswehr wanted to keep secret and the Reichspost had demanded for international use, was made public. This made the machine unusable for the military. In this respect, it had failed for the second time.' Reichspatentamt coordinate corrected to Gitschiner Strasse.
stops.campa: He applies for a patent on the line-by-line scrambling itself, and when the specification is laid open the mechanism becomes public property. The Reichswehr wanted exactly that process kept secret; the Reichspost had demanded it be disclosed, for international traffic. It cannot be both. From the moment it is printed the machine is unusable for the German military, and the men who study these papers afterwards count it the second failure of the project: the first for contacts that would not carry, the second for a secret published by the man who owned it.
suggested_refs: DE385682, the disclosure that Taaks calls the project's second failure
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023

segments.name: Chiffriermaschinen AG: The Company Built on His Patents

stops.name: Berlin, three days of attack at the Foreign Office
stops.date_confidence: attested: Rudolf Schauffler's report on the Scherbius commercial machine, 27-29 June 1923, Politisches Archiv des Auswartigen Amts, quoted in Taaks 2023, p. 174. Scherbius's own presence is not attested and is not claimed: this stop follows the machine, which was demonstrably on the desk, and the campa says so. Coordinate approximates the Foreign Office quarter and is not a verified room.
stops.campa: At the Foreign Office cipher department the commercial machine is put on a desk and worked at for three days at the end of June. Rudolf Schauffler files his report under a title that asks the question plainly, preliminary investigations concerning the Scherbius machine, the question of security. His conclusion is careful and it is not a clearance: attackable in theory, possibly with the help of a purpose-built counterpart machine, though the effort might run high enough that the thing could be used in practice anyway. Scherbius is not recorded as being in the room.
stops.quote: on the basis of theoretical considerations and possibly with the help of a 'counter-machine'
stops.quote_source: Rudolf Schauffler, report on the Scherbius commercial machine, 27-29 June 1923, Politisches Archiv des Auswartigen Amts, translated in Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, p. 174
suggested_refs: Schauffler's report, 'Berichte uber vorlaufige Untersuchungen betr. die Scherbius'sche Maschine (Frage der Sicherheit)', June 1923
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, p. 174

stops.name: Berlin-Tiergarten, Chiffriermaschinen AG founded
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Deutsche Biographie for the founding, with the Steglitzer Strasse 2 address from the Crypto Museum's Scherbius page; de.wikipedia corroborates the founding. The dossier's own framing is kept: he is the crucial inventor, while the documented legal founders and financiers are a broader group.
stops.campa: Chiffriermaschinen Aktiengesellschaft is founded in the Tiergarten district, at Steglitzer Strasse 2, around the patent package that Securitas holds. He is the reason the company exists and he is not the company: the founders and financiers are a broader group with their own lawyers, and the shares are theirs. The commercial Enigma now has a firm behind it, a catalogue, a price, and a sales argument aimed at banks, shipping lines and foreign postal administrations. He is forty-four.
suggested_refs: Handelsregister of ChiMaAG, Landesarchiv Berlin, A Rep 342-02 Nr. 21576 and 21577

stops.name: Berlin, Vossstrasse 18, the inventors outvoted
stops.date_confidence: attested, with the occasion corrected. Taaks 2023, p. 175, distinguishes the preliminary discussion of the capitalists' group from the General Assembly at Vossstrasse 18, where the contract with the Dutch N.V. Internationaal Financierungsbureau was passed 'against the protest of the inventors' group'; the lawyer's remark follows those resolutions, not the preliminary discussion, and the dossier's attribution is amended here. Archive: Landesarchiv Berlin, A Rep 342-02 Nr. 21576/21577. The exact building on Vossstrasse is not located; the coordinate approximates the street.
stops.campa: The general assembly meets on the Vossstrasse eleven weeks after the company was founded, and there the two halves of it come apart in the open. The financiers carry the resolutions, among them a contract with a Dutch finance office, and they carry them against the protest of what the record calls the inventors' group, meaning Scherbius and Ritter. The lawyer for the financiers then puts the value of that contract on the register in a single sentence, and the register is all that survives of the meeting.
stops.quote: The interests of the company are also served by the conclusion of the contract in so far as this makes any litigation with the inventors unnecessary for the company.
stops.quote_source: Statement by the lawyer for the 'capitalists' group' following the resolutions of the ChiMaAG General Assembly, Vossstrasse 18, 24 September 1923; Handelsregister ChiMaAG, Landesarchiv Berlin, translated in Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, p. 175
suggested_refs: Landesarchiv Berlin, A Rep 342-02 Nr. 21576 and 21577, the ChiMaAG commercial register
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, p. 175

stops.name: Berlin, two pages in the Elektrotechnische Zeitschrift
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, with pagination: 'Enigma Chiffriermaschine', Elektrotechnische Zeitschrift vol. 44, nos. 47/48, pp. 1035-1036, 29 November 1923 (Deutsche Biographie; Crypto Museum's Enigma history). The text itself was NOT obtained in this research: no digitization, translation or reprint of the full article could be located, which makes it the single most valuable missing document for this subject. Coordinate approximates the journal's Berlin publishing quarter and is not a located address.
stops.campa: He publishes in the Elektrotechnische Zeitschrift, the journal every German electrical engineer reads, under the title Enigma Chiffriermaschine: two pages in the issue of the twenty-ninth of November, explaining why communications need protecting and how a machine can do the protecting. It is the fullest public statement he ever makes about his own invention. It gives away nothing of wiring or procedure that would compromise a military user, and it is the only extended text in his own voice on the subject that anyone since has been able to find.
suggested_refs: Arthur Scherbius, 'Enigma Chiffriermaschine', Elektrotechnische Zeitschrift 44 (1923), nos. 47/48, pp. 1035-1036, untranslated and unreprinted

stops.name: Stockholm, the machine shown to the postal administrations of the world
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year only (en.wikipedia; Crypto Museum): ChiMaAG displayed an Enigma at the Universal Postal Union Congress at Stockholm in 1924. The congress venue within Stockholm is not identified and the coordinate marks the city centre, a stated gap; the month is a placeholder. The delivery figures are Taaks's list for the period: two glow-lamp machines (Enigma B) to the Swedish General Staff, twelve commercial machines to Sentel in Prague, ten Funkschlussel C to the naval command.
stops.campa: The company shows the machine at the Universal Postal Union congress in Stockholm, in front of the postal administrations of the world and, less openly, their military and intelligence services. Two glow-lamp machines go to the Swedish General Staff, a dozen commercial machines to a buyer in Prague, and various services borrow examples to look at. The exhibition does not create the civilian market the company needs. It creates something else: a machine that every interested government now knows exists and can obtain.
stops.quote: It has already been proposed to use for ciphering of a clear text and for deciphering machines which either type the ciphered letters in a similar manner to that of a typewriting machine or which produce a ciphered perforated cable tape or operate an indicating device.
stops.quote_source: Arthur Scherbius, US Patent 1,657,411, 'Ciphering Machine', opening of the specification; German priority 11 February 1922, US filing 6 February 1923, granted 24 January 1928 and assigned to Chiffriermaschinen AG
suggested_refs: US Patent 1,657,411, the machine's legal passage abroad
Taaks 2023's delivery list for 1924-25, the best-attested record of who actually received machines
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023
US Patent Office, specification of US 1,657,411

stops.name: Berlin-Wannsee, the house on the Lindenstrasse
stops.date_confidence: attested, with the dossier's largest geographic error corrected. gazette-berlin.de: 'Zum Vermogen gehorte auch ein Grundstuck in der Lindenstrasse 5/6, auf dem sich Scherbius und Ritter Hauser fur ihre Familien bauten'; de.wikipedia dates the move to September 1924. The dossier had the house and the works swapped, putting the residence at Konigstrasse 40. Konigstrasse 40 is the WORKS (52.4178, 13.1457); Lindenstrasse 5/6 is the two family houses, and this coordinate is Lindenstrasse 5, 14109 Berlin.
stops.campa: In September the couple move into a newly built house on the plot at Lindenstrasse 5 and 6, land the two partners hold together, each raising a house for his own family a few streets from the works. He is forty-five, married seven years, and this is the height of everything he will ever have: a firm, a company, a minority holding in his own patents. The circle that comes to the door is engineers and, by the family's account, people out of artistic, literary and political life.
suggested_refs: Lindenstrasse 5/6, Berlin-Wannsee, the two houses built by Scherbius and Ritter; no plaque or marker there could be confirmed

stops.name: Berlin, the navy becomes a customer
stops.date_confidence: the muddiest procurement claim in the record, carried unresolved. Taaks 2023, listing what was built and delivered around 1924-25, gives '10 machines Funkschlussel C to the naval command'. The Crypto Museum says the Navy purchased Funkschlussel C, a naval version of the commercial Enigma C, in 1926, with no quantity. The dossier's 'fifty ordered 1925, delivered from 1926' is supported by nothing reached and is not adopted. Month is a placeholder; the Bendlerblock pin is the seat of naval and army procurement, not a documented meeting place.
stops.campa: The Reichsmarine buys. Ten machines of the naval type, the Funkschlussel C, a version of the commercial Enigma adapted for the fleet, go to the naval command, and the German state that would not buy the patents in 1920 becomes a customer of the company that owns them now. The first standing military order for a machine of his design comes six years after a ministry told him to sell it abroad. The quantities and the year are the muddiest numbers in the whole record: ten against fifty, 1925 against 1926.
suggested_refs: Funkschlussel C, the Reichsmarine's naval adaptation of the commercial Enigma
sources: Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023
dossier procurement summary, unsupported as to quantity

stops.name: Berlin, the Post Minister arrested
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Deutsche Biographie for Hofle's arrest on 10 February 1925 and for the affair's contact with ChiMaAG's financial dealings, including a bank loan connected to the businessman Hermkes, who resigns eleven days later. The broad contours of the Barmat scandal are standard Weimar political history. Coordinate approximates the Reichspost ministry quarter.
stops.campa: Anton Hofle, Reich Post Minister, is arrested on the tenth of February in the embezzlement and bribery investigation that Berlin will spend the rest of the year calling the Barmat affair. None of it has anything to do with rotors or ciphers, and it is what breaks the company. The web of loans and favours runs through the Reichspost, and one strand of it runs through Chiffriermaschinen AG: a bank loan tied to a businessman named Hermkes, who resigns eleven days after the arrest.
suggested_refs: The Barmat-Kutisker scandal of 1925 and the Reichspost credit network
sources: standard accounts of the 1925 Barmat scandal

stops.name: Berlin, the 1918 patent published at last
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the Crypto Museum patent index: DE416219, filed 23 February 1918, published 8 July 1925. The priority contest noted in the campa is likewise from the Crypto Museum's patent index, which records ChiMaAG's 1927 acquisition of Koch's Dutch patents and names the Dutch naval officers R. P. C. Spengler and Theo A. van Hengel as having conceived the rotor principle as early as 1915. Reichspatentamt coordinate as corrected throughout.
stops.campa: Seven years and four months after it was filed, the foundational patent is published as DE416219. The priority stands on the public record now for anyone to read: February 1918, ahead of the Dutch filings later credited with the same idea, and three years behind two Dutch naval officers who conceived the rotor principle in 1915 and did not patent it. The document appears in the same fortnight in which the company that owns it is being examined in the Reichstag. He owns a minority of it.
suggested_refs: DE416219 as published, 8 July 1925
The contested rotor priority: Spengler and van Hengel 1915, Koch, Damm, Hebern, Scherbius

stops.name: Berlin, the Reichstag committee and a marriage contract
stops.date_confidence: the Reichstag Barmat investigatory committee's examination of ChiMaAG's dealings with Hofle and the Reichspost is attested for July 1925 by the dossier's summary, corroborated in general terms by standard accounts of the scandal; the 15 July date is the dossier's and is not independently confirmed. The separation of property is [R], a family-document reconstruction with only the year 1925 known, and it is folded in here rather than given a stop of its own.
stops.campa: The Reichstag's Barmat investigating committee takes up Chiffriermaschinen AG's dealings with the Post Minister and the Reichspost, and the newspapers carry it. A cipher-machine firm whose whole commercial argument is discretion is named in the national press in connection with a bribery scandal, and the company's first corporate structure does not survive it. In the same year the Scherbius household separates its property, Elisabeth taking the Wannsee house and two accounts, which will turn out to protect nothing at all.
suggested_refs: Press coverage of the Reichstag Barmat committee, July 1925
sources: dossier summary of the Barmat committee and of the 1925 separation of property

stops.name: Berlin, thirteen printing machines ordered and cancelled
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The Reichswehr order for thirteen printing Enigmas in April 1926, cancelled two months later, rests on the dossier's summary of the procurement record and was not independently corroborated; it is tagged [R] and kept because the printing line is otherwise invisible in the sources. The Bendlerblock pin is the institutional seat, not a documented location for this transaction.
stops.campa: The Reichswehr orders thirteen printing Enigmas in April and cancels the order in June. Two months, and no reason that has come down. The printing machine is the line he has worked since 1919, the one that puts the cipher onto paper without a second operator reading lamps aloud, and it is the line that never finds a buyer. The cruder machine, the one with the lamps, is the one the army will come back for. By this date he has been trying to sell a cipher machine to the German state for nine years.
suggested_refs: The printing Enigma line, developed from 1919 and never adopted
sources: dossier summary of the documented procurement record, uncorroborated

stops.name: Berlin-Tiergarten, on the board of a company with nothing to distribute
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the exact years. The dossier's corporate-record summary places him on ChiMaAG's management board in 1927-1928 rather than continuously since 1923; independent sources confirm a board role in this period but not the bracketing years, so the stop is tagged conservatively to the start year with a placeholder month. The absence of any dividend is from the same summary.
stops.campa: Corporate records put him on the management board of Chiffriermaschinen AG, at the Steglitzer Strasse offices, in these two years rather than continuously since the founding. The company has been stabilized and continues. The accumulated losses mean there is no dividend. He has invented the machine, handed over the patents for a minority holding, sat through the scandal, and arrived on the board of the firm at the point where the firm has nothing to hand out. No money from the Enigma reaches him at any moment of his life.
suggested_refs: ChiMaAG board records for 1927-1928, per the dossier's corporate-record summary
sources: dossier corporate-record summary, board dates uncorroborated

stops.name: Berlin, four hundred machines for the Army
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, precise and thinly sourced. The order for 400 Enigma I machines on 17 May 1927 comes from the dossier's procurement summary, corroborated only in general terms by Bletchley Park's institutional history that the German military adopted the machine; the date and quantity were not independently verified and the claim is tagged [R]. Bendlerblock pin as institutional seat.
stops.campa: The Army orders four hundred Enigma I machines. It is the largest order of his lifetime and the moment a commercial venture turns into a state supply contract, and the record for it is thinner than its importance: a date, a number, a summary. Service introduction across the German forces, the versions with plugboards and extra wheels, the tens of thousands of machines, all of that comes later and he sees none of it. What he sees in May 1927 is an order for four hundred.
suggested_refs: The Enigma I, the Army machine developed from the commercial line

stops.name: Berlin, a switch that works in a vacuum
stops.date_confidence: attested: US Patent 1,875,765, 'Vacuum Switch', German priority 1 July 1927, US filing 28 May 1928, granted posthumously 6 September 1932, specification text read directly. The January 1929 filing mentioned in the campa is DE541702, electromagnets used in typewriters and ciphering machines for printing, filed 30 January 1929 per the Crypto Museum patent index. The patent-office pin stands for the German priority filing.
stops.campa: He files, in the same summer, a patent with nothing to do with cipher at all: a vacuum switch, contacts of high-melting-point metal working inside an evacuated vessel, and a way around the arcing that ruins such switches under heavy load. It is granted in the United States three years after his death. In January 1929 he files once more, on electromagnets for printing in typewriters and in ciphering machines. That application, filed on the thirtieth of January, is the last he signs.
stops.quote: It is known to allow contacts of metals of high melting points to work in vacuum vessels or in vessels filled with neutral gases. It has been found that with such switches there is a tendency at heavy loads for arcs to form in the interior of the vessel, whereby a limit is set to their employment.
stops.quote_source: Arthur Scherbius, US Patent 1,875,765, 'Vacuum Switch', specification (German priority 1 July 1927; granted 6 September 1932, after his death)
suggested_refs: US Patent 1,875,765; DE541702, filed 30 January 1929, his last application
sources: US Patent Office, specification of US 1,875,765

stops.name: Berlin, a boy comes from a children's home
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day not. de.wikipedia: 'Elisabeth adoptierte 1930 ein Heimkind, das die Eheleute im Januar 1929 bei sich aufgenommen hatten.' The dossier's 15 January is unsourced and is dropped; so is the child's name 'Rainer Scherbius', which is unattested in anything reached. The institution is unidentified, so the coordinate is central Berlin and is a stated gap.
stops.campa: In January a boy comes from a children's home to the house in Wannsee, and the couple begin the proceedings to adopt him. Arthur does not live to see the papers finished. Elisabeth completes the adoption alone in 1930, a widow of thirty-four with the wreckage of a firm around her. Which home the boy came from is not recorded anywhere reachable, nor the day he arrived, nor, in any source that can be checked, the name he was given. The record of this family is thinnest exactly where families keep their own paper.
suggested_refs: Berlin adoption records for 1929-1930, not located

stops.name: Berlin-Wannsee, the carriage and the wall
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, with the mechanism corrected. The dossier had a runaway carriage pressing him against a wall as a bystander; the sources have him driving. gazette-berlin.de: 'Im Mai 1929 prallte der Unternehmer mit seiner Kutsche gegen eine Mauer und verstarb an seinen inneren Verletzungen.' de.wikipedia: he died 'nachdem er die Kontrolle uber einen Pferdewagen verloren hatte'. Deutsche Biographie: 'dagger (Unfall) 13.5.1929 Berlin'. A rival claim of suicide after business failure is attributed to Bengt Beckman via Friedrich L. Bauer's chapter 'Scherbius und die ENIGMA'; the Springer chapter is behind a login wall and was not read, so the claim is recorded and not adjudicated. The street of the accident is not established; the pin is the Wannsee works.
stops.campa: He is driving a horse-drawn carriage in Wannsee on the thirteenth of May when he loses control of it and strikes a wall. The injuries are internal and he dies the same day, fifty years old, his fiftieth birthday six months behind him and his last patent application three and a half months behind that. There is no police finding in any reachable file, no contemporaneous account of the street or the hour, and no agreement in the later literature on whether the accident was an accident.
suggested_refs: Hannoverscher Kurier, 17 May 1929, death notice, digitized at digitale-sammlungen.gwlb.de and not opened in this research
Friedrich L. Bauer, 'Scherbius und die ENIGMA', Springer, paywalled, carrier of the suicide claim

stops.name: Berlin-Wannsee, the cemetery on the Lindenstrasse
stops.date_confidence: the burial in the Lindenstrasse cemetery at Wannsee is attested by gazette-berlin.de, which also states plainly that 'sein Grab existiert nicht mehr'; the underlying civil burial record was not located and the date of the funeral is not recorded anywhere reached, so the stop carries the date of death. The coordinate approximates the Wannsee Lindenstrasse cemetery and is not a plot. The obituary quoted is dated 14 July 1929, two months after the burial.
stops.campa: He is buried in the cemetery on the Lindenstrasse in Wannsee, a few minutes' walk from the house he built and from the works where the machine was developed. The day of the funeral is not recorded, and neither is the plot. Two months afterwards a colleague publishes a notice in an engineering journal, the only sustained description of his character that anybody wrote down. The grave does not exist any more: no stone, no marker, and no restoration of it ever proposed.
stops.quote: Luck rarely helped this man in his search for new paths. No matter how often disappointment weighed down his heavy, serious character, the belief in the final success of an idea that was recognized as right never left him. Failures, therefore, could not paralyze him, but only spurred him on to renewed efforts.
stops.quote_source: Heinrich Meyer-Delius, obituary notice, Elektrotechnik und Maschinenbau vol. 47, issue 28, 14 July 1929, p. 610f; English translation by Jim Rawlinson, epigraph to Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023
suggested_refs: Friedhof Lindenstrasse, Berlin-Wannsee, where the grave no longer exists
sources: Heinrich Meyer-Delius, Elektrotechnik und Maschinenbau 47/28 (1929), via Taaks 2023

stops.name: Berlin-Wannsee, the firms outlive the name
stops.date_confidence: posthumous stop: Scherbius died 13 May 1929 and was present at none of this. The 1935 takeover of Chiffriermaschinen AG by Rudolf Heimsoeth and Elsbeth Rinke, and the successor firm's role as principal supplier to the German armed forces, are attested by the Crypto Museum's ChiMaAG page; the continued manufacture of thermostats and switches at the Wannsee works is from the Crypto Museum's Scherbius page. The quoted judgement is the Neue Deutsche Biographie's, written much later. Month is a placeholder; the pin is the Konigstrasse works.
stops.campa: The firms outlive him and take his name off. Chiffriermaschinen AG passes in 1935 to Rudolf Heimsoeth and Elsbeth Rinke and becomes Heimsoeth und Rinke, which supplies the German armed forces for the whole production life of the machine, while the Wannsee works go on making thermostats and switches for decades. No prototype from 1918 survives anywhere. The patent does. And the standard German biographical reference, writing long afterwards, does not claim to know how much of the machine's later development was his.
stops.quote_source: Deutsche Biographie (Neue Deutsche Biographie), entry gnd127822089, on Scherbius's role in the Enigma's further development: 'not yet fully clarified'
suggested_refs: Heimsoeth & Rinke, successor manufacturer of the Enigma
The Science Museum Group's three-ring Enigma in its oak transit case, catalogued against an authority record naming Scherbius as designer
Claus Taaks, 'Scherbius and the Enigma', HistoCrypt 2023, the modern archival reassessment
sources: Science Museum Group collection record, 'Arthur Scherbius'
